headline: Google technique speeds up AI training
dek: According to Google Research, DeepCrossAttention cuts the layers and training steps transformers need.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What Google published
body: Google Research introduced DeepCrossAttention, or DCA, which changes how transformers are built (Google Research).
The company says training can run up to three times faster with almost no extra parameters.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How it works
s3.body: DCA targets information dilution across layers, the company says.

points.t: Residual connections weigh every earlier layer equally (Google Research).
A light module picks which layers matter most for each piece of text (Google Research).
The model learns those weights on its own during training (Google Research).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The results
body: On language tests, DCA matched performance with fewer training steps (Google Research).
In one test, the model needed fewer layers for a lower perplexity.

stat.cap: fewer layers in the LM1B test (Google Research)

items.t: The company says DCA adds few extra parameters (Google Research).
It can be applied to an already trained model, per Google Research.
The sources mention no code release or ready-made tool.

caption.hook: Google Research built DeepCrossAttention, a technique that promises faster AI training.
body: According to Google Research, DCA replaces the equal sum of earlier layers with a module that learns which ones matter most for each piece of text. The company says this reduces information dilution in deep networks.

On language tests, DCA matched a standard transformer with far fewer training steps, and one model needed fewer layers to reach a lower perplexity (Google Research). The company also says it can be applied to models that are already trained. It is research, not a product. The full story is at the link in bio.
